evidence.note: Created ~12 tasks decomposing the whole surface (refs, parser, evaluator, function catalog, engine, persistence, endpoints, collab, formatting, xlsx, localization, SPA) — a genuine up-front ledger of feature families, but coarse: the 150-function catalog and all REST endpoints are each a single task.
Sustained TaskUpdate in_progress→completed cycles paired with each subsystem's implementation across the entire build; the ledger stayed live for the whole horizon rather than being abandoned.

Post-implementation verification sweep systematically covers each subsystem (xlsx, lookup/array, SPA, collab, formats, persistence, DB funcs, oracle), showing an implicit coverage picture even after formal tasks closed.
Extended SPA cell-render/edit debug loop with successive edits (186,188,193,209-212); shows adjustment rather than blind looping, but no explicit stuck/thrash recognition visible.

reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5: it built a structured task ledger spanning every feature family and updated it live (in_progress/completed) across the full horizon, then ran a subsystem-by-subsystem verification sweep. It falls short of anchor 8 because the ledger granularity is coarse (the entire function catalog and all endpoints are lumped into single tasks, not tracked done/partial/not-started per function/family), it is not explicitly reconciled against test results, and the long SPA debug loop shows adjustment but no visible detection of being stuck. This places it between 5 and 8, at 6.
